diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Atrial fibrillation with high thrombo‑embolic risk on warfarin
supporting_evidence_verified: High CHA2DS2‑VASc (age >80, HTN, DM, CKD, IHD, OSA)
evidence_gaps: History of prior stroke/TIA or systemic embolism

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Metabolic acidosis secondary to advanced CKD
supporting_evidence_verified: CO2 total 20.2 mmol/L indicating metabolic acidosis
eGFR <10 mL/min/1.73m² consistent with uremic acidosis
evidence_gaps: Whether patient is already on bicarbonate therapy
concerns: Probability lower than expected for a near‑inevitable ESRD complication

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: CKD‑related anemia (EPO deficiency) possibly compounded by iron deficiency
supporting_evidence_verified: Active problem list includes moderate anemia
Stage 5 CKD commonly causes anemia of EPO deficiency
concerns: Exact aetiology (pure EPO deficiency vs iron deficiency vs anemia of chronic disease) not defined

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Obstructive sleep apnea contributing to resistant hypertension & atrial fibrillation
evidence_gaps: Blood pressure response to CPAP therapy
concerns: Impact on current presentation not quantified

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Possible cholestatic / hepatic dysfunction (unexplained urinary bilirubin)
concerns: Evidence insufficient to label as cholestatic liver disease
Could be false‑positive urine dipstick or hemolysis

consistency_checks.detail: eGFR, creatinine, proteinuria all align with stage 5 CKD
Warfarin listed without current INR; cannot confirm therapeutic range
Urine ketones present but no diagnosis addresses this abnormality

critical_findings_missed: Urine ketones 12 mg/dL (no diagnosis directly explains)
Urine bilirubin (explained only by a questionable hepatic diagnosis)
top_concerns: Probability weighting underestimates the dominance of CKD and overestimates peripheral diagnoses
Insufficient data for hepatic dysfunction (no serum LFTs, imaging)
Missing anticoagulation monitoring (INR) and digoxin level
Omission of high‑impact conditions: stage‑1 NSCLC and hypertriglyceridemia
recommended_primary: Advanced CKD stage 5 secondary to diabetic & hypertensive nephropathy
review_summary: The differential captures the core renal pathology, atrial fibrillation, metabolic acidosis, and anemia, but under‑weights CKD, omits the curable stage‑1 NSCLC and hypertriglyceridemia, and fails to explain ketonuria. Probability adjustments and additional work‑up (INR, LFTs, digoxin level, lipid panel, cancer staging) are needed to refine the plan.
